chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazala ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Abu Al-Jaroud, who said:

A man asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a louse while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done.' He said, 'So what is its expiation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no expiation for it.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَر: Abu Ja'far (Imam Al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a louse while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) clarifies that while killing a louse while in Ihram is considered a minor fault ('bi'sa ma sana'), it does not incur a specific fidyah (expiation). This ruling highlights the distinction in Shia jurisprudence between larger game animals, which require compensation, and smaller insects like lice, whose killing is discouraged but not penalized with a ritual fine, reflecting the principle of ease in ritual consecration.
